_meta.what_this_is: A worker pool of fixed size and a stream of requests, each targeting one of two downstream dependencies: X, which has hung (every X request holds its worker for the whole run and never releases it), and Y, which is healthy (a Y request completes instantly, releasing its worker at once). With one SHARED pool, the hung X requests pile up and hold every worker, so healthy Y requests find no free worker and are starved -- one bad dependency takes down an unrelated one. With BULKHEADS, the pool is partitioned so X can hold at most its share; Y keeps its own workers and stays served.
_meta.data_is: A FIXTURE. The arrival order, pool size, and bulkhead caps are hand-authored so the shared pool serves 0 of the Y requests while the bulkhead pool serves all of them. Every admission decision is computed in bulkhead.py.
_meta.format: arrivals: request targets in order; workers: total pool size; bulkhead: {X, Y} per-dependency caps summing to workers.
